raw_response:
I am keeping stevia on all 1.1 mu this year. My land is small, so I do not want to take risks changing crops. Stevia has been my usual way, and I know how to manage it. I watch what other people nearby do. If the spring stays normal, I will plant around late April after the ground warms. I will buy local improved seedlings, not the cheapest ones, because if the stand is poor on such a small plot, I lose too much. Fertilizer I will use, but not too heavy. I cannot throw money around, and pumping water also costs money. I plan to put a base fertilizer before planting, then one topdressing after the plants are established and growing fast. If the leaves look weak later, I may add a little more nitrogen, but I do not want too much or the plants grow soft and lodging becomes a problem. Since I have well water, I will irrigate when the field is dry, especially after transplanting and during the strong growth period. Pesticide I will not spray by habit. I will check the field first. If weeds come badly, I handle them early, and if insects show up, I will buy a simple product from town. Family labor is enough for most of this, and for 1.1 mu I do not expect to hire much help.
